topic: How the Golden Gate Bridge cables hold it up
visual_style: Photorealistic cinematic film still, natural daylight, real materials and textures, shallow depth of field, bright orange steel against blue water and soft fog
world: San Francisco's Golden Gate strait today: cool morning fog lifting to clear golden afternoon light over blue water
through_line: the orange main cable, from its outside to the thousands of wires inside it

blocks.narration: Eighty thousand miles of wire. That is what holds this bridge up, enough to wrap around the whole Earth three times.

captions.hook_line: The Golden Gate Bridge hangs from 80,000 miles of wire 🌉
captions.body: Each of the Golden Gate Bridge's two main cables is about 36 inches thick and holds 27,572 steel wires, about 80,000 miles of wire in all, enough to circle the Earth more than three times. The wires were spun in place across the strait before the deck was hung, and so many wires share the load that a few breaks do not matter.
captions.comment_prompt: Would you rather cross on one solid steel bar or 27,572 thin wires?
